title: Method References to Existing Behavior
subtopics: Decomposing large methods into smaller units
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of method references to existing behavior and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—instance method calls—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study method references to existing behavior with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you give reusable behavior a clear input/output contract that can be tested independently. In this lesson, focus on instance method calls and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect instance method calls with methods that return values before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Decomposing large methods into smaller units
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

items.title: Preparing for lambda expressions
items.text: A lambda provides an implementation of a functional interface. Prefer a named helper when it improves readability, and avoid unexpected shared-state mutation in callbacks.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
